children.title: 1.0 MOBILIZATION ADVANCE
children.content:
Interest bearing Mobilization Advance (Rate of interest @ 7.70% per annum) shall be paid as per the
General conditions of Contract in minimum two instalments against BG for 110% of the value of the
advance applicable GST.
children.summary:
This text outlines the terms for a **Mobilization Advance** payment. The key information includes:

*   **Interest Rate:** The advance is subject to an annual interest rate of 7.70%.
*   **Payment Structure:** Funds will be disbursed in at least two separate installments.
*   **Governing Terms:** The process is governed by the project's General Conditions of Contract.
*   **Security Requirement:** To receive the advance, the recipient must provide a Bank Guarantee (BG).
*   **Guarantee Value:** The Bank Guarantee must cover 110% of the advance value plus any applicable GST.

children.title: 2.0 SECURED ADVANCE ON MATERIALS
children.content:
Secured Advance shall be paid as per the General Conditions of Contract. However, no Secured Advance
shall be paid against the material wherever Milestone Payment has been recommended on receipt and
acceptance of material at site.
children.summary:
The provided text outlines the conditions for issuing a **Secured Advance** for materials. It contains two primary rules:

1.  **Standard Procedure:** Payments for Secured Advances are generally governed by the terms set forth in the General Conditions of Contract.
2.  **Exception:** A Secured Advance will not be granted for materials if the project already includes a **Milestone Payment** triggered by the delivery and acceptance of those same materials at the site.

In short, the text ensures that contractors do not receive duplicate payments (both an advance and a milestone payment) for the same supply of materials.

children.summary:
This text outlines the progressive payment terms for a construction contract, categorized by the nature of the work. Payments are released against "running account bills" certified by the Engineer-in-charge, subject to necessary deductions.

Key information includes:

*   **Civil & Piling Works:** Payments for soil investigation, piling installation, and testing are milestone-based, typically retaining 5% until the final completion certificate is issued.
*   **Underground (U/G) Piping:** Detailed payment breakdowns are provided for Carbon Steel piping. Terms vary based on whether the pipes are "Free Issue" (supplied by the owner) or supplied by the contractor, with milestones for fabrication, NDT/testing, laying, and backfilling.
*   **Structural Steel & Architectural Works:** Covers fabrication (at site or off-site), erection, and painting. Off-site fabrication requires a Bank Guarantee for materials. Architectural items like doors, roofing, and modular furniture are paid primarily upon receipt of material (60–75%) and installation (20–25%).
*   **Composite & Miscellaneous Items:** Specific schedules exist for RCC work, brickwork, and reinforcement steel. 

In almost all categories, a final **5% retention** is released only upon the issuance of a formal completion certificate.

The provided text summarizes administrative and financial terms found in a formal construction contract, specifically an Annexure to the Special Conditions of Contract (SCC). The information is categorized into four main areas:

*   **Administrative Metadata:** Identifies the document as page 2 of 35 within the SCC annexure.
*   **Mobilization Advance:** Outlines terms for early funding, including a 7.70% annual interest rate, disbursement in at least two installments, and the requirement of a Bank Guarantee covering 110% of the advance plus GST.
*   **Secured Advance:** Details rules for material-based advances, noting that these are prohibited if the contract already includes a "Milestone Payment" for the delivery of the same materials to prevent duplicate billing.
*   **Progressive Payment Schedule:** Defines how "running account bills" are paid across different work types (Civil, Piling, Piping, Structural, and Architectural). Payments are released based on specific milestones—such as fabrication, testing, and installation—with a standard 5% retention held until the final completion certificate is issued. Off-site fabrication specifically requires a Bank Guarantee for material security.

This document outlines the structured **Payment Terms** for various engineering and construction works under an Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. (IOCL) contract. It details a milestone-based payment schedule where total compensation is released progressively upon the completion of specific technical stages.

Key categories of work include:
*   **Piping & Equipment:** Covers fabrication, erection, and testing of above-ground piping, heat exchangers, pumps, and vessels.
*   **Electrical & Instrumentation:** Payments are split between material supply (typically 65–95%), installation, and loop checking/testing.
*   **Specialized Structures:** Detailed schedules for Tankages, Spheres, Mounded Bullets, and Heaters, including design, supply, and site fabrication.
*   **Pipeline Works:** Includes onshore laying, HDD (Horizontal Directional Drilling), and Cathodic Protection.
*   **Support Services:** Covers NDT (Non-Destructive Testing), stress relieving, painting, insulation, and refractory works.

**General Payment Structure:**
Most items follow a similar percentage breakdown:
1.  **Supply/Receipt:** 40–70% upon material acceptance.
2.  **Execution:** 15–45% for fabrication, erection, and welding.
3.  **Testing:** 5–15% for hydro-testing, NDT, and alignment.
4.  **Mechanical Completion:** 2% (standard for many items).
5.  **Final Closure:** A final **5%** is reserved until the issuance of the final completion certificate.

This document details the structured **Payment Terms** for engineering and construction contracts under Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. (IOCL). It establishes a milestone-based compensation framework where payments are released progressively as specific technical stages are completed.

The scope of work is categorized into several key areas:
*   **Mechanical & Piping:** Fabrication, erection, and testing of piping, vessels, and heat exchangers.
*   **Electrical & Instrumentation:** Split between material supply and installation/testing.
*   **Specialized Infrastructure:** Design and fabrication of tanks, spheres, mounded bullets, and heaters.
*   **Pipeline & Support Services:** Onshore laying, HDD, NDT, painting, and insulation.

**General Payment Structure:**
Payments typically follow a four-stage breakdown:
1.  **Supply/Receipt:** 40–70% upon material acceptance at the site.
2.  **Execution:** 15–45% for fabrication, welding, and erection.
3.  **Testing:** 5–15% for hydro-testing and alignment.
4.  **Completion:** A standard 2% is released at mechanical completion, with the final **5%** withheld until the issuance of the final completion certificate.

This structure ensures financial accountability by aligning contractor cash flow with verified project milestones.

This text outlines the standard payment terms and schedules for pipeline laying and associated infrastructure projects. It serves as an annexure to the Special Conditions of Contract (SCC), detailing how payments are disbursed across different stages of work.

Key information includes:

*   **Work Categories:** Specific payment breakdowns are provided for submarine pipeline laying, SPM & PLEM system installation, pre-commissioning, pipe coating/transportation, and dumpsite management.
*   **Milestone-Based Payments:** Payments are generally released in percentages linked to milestones such as mobilization (typically 20%), completion of physical installation (50–65%), and submission of "As-Built" drawings (5%).
*   **Final Retention:** Most categories reserve a final 5% payment until the issuance of a completion certificate and the resolution of all defects.
*   **Administrative Provisions:** The text allows for the modification of terms based on work quantum and provides guidelines for material handling and lump-sum items.
*   **Deductions:** All progress payments are subject to statutory deductions, including Indian Income Tax (TDS) and other contractual withholdings.
*   **Flexibility:** The Engineer-in-Charge has the authority to approve further price break-ups for progressive payments on lump-sum items.

This text details the administrative and financial frameworks for an Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. (IOCL) construction contract, specifically found within the **Annexure to the Special Conditions of Contract (SCC)**.

The information is categorized into three primary areas:

1.  **Financial Advances:** It specifies terms for **Mobilization Advances** (7.70% interest, 110% Bank Guarantee requirement) and **Secured Advances**, which are prohibited if milestone payments for the same materials already exist to prevent double-billing.
2.  **Payment Structure:** The document establishes a **milestone-based payment system** for various engineering sectors, including Civil, Mechanical, Piping, Electrical, and Pipeline laying. Payments are typically released in stages: Supply/Receipt (40–70%), Execution/Installation (15–45%), and Testing (5–15%).
3.  **Retention and Compliance:** A final **5% retention** is held until the final completion certificate is issued. All payments are subject to statutory deductions like Income Tax (TDS).

Ultimately, the text serves as a 35-page regulatory roadmap designed to align contractor cash flow with verified technical progress and material security.
